issues.title: [API] Статус аккаунта — «Активен», обновление API положительно из инфтерфейса; новые серверы не появляются, конфигурации не скачиваются 1100, подключение не работает на любых устройствах по ключу VPN
issues.body:
Описание ошибки
После тестирования кастомной сборки с функцией автоматической смены локации каждые 2 часа клиент перестал получать актуальные данные о серверах и конфигурациях. Статус аккаунта по-прежнему отображается как «Активен», обновление API происходит положительно если верить интерфейсу, однако при попытке подключиться к любой локации выполняется бесконечное подключение, при скачивании конфигов выдает ошибку 1100.
Список серверов остается устаревшим (доступно лишь 10–14 серверов, новые не появляются). Проблема воспроизводится на любом устройстве при использовании того же аккаунта/ключа. В службе поддержки после описания проблемы, через 5 минут сообщили, что аккаунт был заблокирован за «злоупотребление API». Хотелось бы уточнить: дейстсвительно ли моя учетная запись заблокирована или это я что то не так сделал и попал в баг, потому что я использовал офф приложение просто доделав ему функцию рандомного выбора страны и переключения каждые 2 часа, я руками зачастую чаще переключаюсь на VPN так как он то нужен то нет для серфинга сайтов.

Ответ технической поддержки
Здравствуйте!
На вашем аккаунте зафиксирована активность, создающая повышенную нагрузку на инфраструктуру Amnezia Premium. Такая активность возникает при использовании стороннего программного обеспечения, выполняющего автоматические запросы к API, частые проверки доступности серверов или повторное получение конфигураций. (что то я очень сомневаюсь в ддосе по API, больше поверю, что я что то не так сделал в запросе но я вроде ничего не изменял)
Amnezia Premium предназначен для использования с официально поддерживаемыми приложениями и способами подключения. Мы не гарантируем корректную работу сервиса при использовании стороннего программного обеспечения, которое не поддерживается Amnezia. Некоторые сторонние приложения и автоматизированные инструменты могут выполнять фоновые запросы, многократные проверки доступности серверов или другие операции, создающие повышенную нагрузку на инфраструктуру и API сервиса. Такая активность может автоматически определяться системами защиты как подозрительная и приводить к ограничениям аккаунта независимо от намерений пользователя.
Использование подобных инструментов является нарушением Политики конфиденциальности и приемлемого использования сервиса. В целях обеспечения стабильности и безопасности сервиса подобная активность приводит к ограничениям доступа, а при её повторении — к дополнительным защитным мерам в соответствии с действующими условиями использования сервиса. (я не получал никаких уведомлений или предпосылок к блокировкам или что либо и даже сейчас из учетной записи не понятно заблокирован я или нет)
Обращаем внимание: в связи с данным нарушением пересмотр ограничений, компенсации или иные решения по вашему обращению предоставлены не будут.

Ответ технической поддержки
Возможен ли разбан?
Могу ли я купить ключ на ту же почту и пользоваться?
Здравствуйте!
Покупка новой подписки не гарантирует работоспособность. Разбан за деньги не предоставляем.

issues.title: [Windows][Premium] Tunnel DNS rewrites chatgpt.com / api.openai.com to a proxy that drops ~70% of TLS handshakes (Codex fails with os error 10053)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
On Amnezia Premium, the DNS inside the tunnel resolves OpenAI domains not to their real Cloudflare addresses but to a proxy IP. That proxy fails most TLS handshakes, so OpenAI Codex constantly drops with:
`stream disconnected before completion: IO error: An established connection was aborted by the software in your host machine. (os error 10053)`

Browsing other sites (google.com etc.) through the same tunnel works fine.

**Environment**
- AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0, Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Amnezia Premium, exit Finland (exit IP in AS9009 M247, Helsinki); same result on 3 other countries
- Protocols tested: AmneziaWG and VLESS — same result
- "Use AmneziaDNS" is OFF, custom DNS set to 1.1.1.1 / 1.0.0.1 — ignored, the tunnel interface still gets `100.64.0.1, 8.8.4.4` (see also #2655)

**What happens**
1. Inside the tunnel `chatgpt.com`, `api.openai.com`, `auth.openai.com` resolve to `57.129.144.160` (AS16276 OVH, GB), after reconnect — `216.152.150.132`.
2. The same rewritten answer comes back even when querying `1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8` or `9.9.9.9` directly — plain DNS on port 53 is intercepted in the tunnel.
3. Real addresses via DoH (cloudflare-dns.com): `chatgpt.com` → `104.18.32.47, 172.64.155.209`, `api.openai.com` → `172.66.0.243, 162.159.140.245`.

**Measurements (curl, same tunnel, same moment)**
| Target | Success |
|---|---|
| `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` via proxy IP (AmneziaWG) | 2 / 10 |
| same via proxy IP (VLESS) | 5 / 15 |
| `https://api.openai.com/v1/models` via proxy IP | 1–2 / 4–5 |
| same endpoints via real IP (`curl --resolve chatgpt.com:443:104.18.32.47`) | 15 / 15, 5 / 5 |

Failures are `curl: (35) schannel: failed to receive handshake, SSL/TLS connection failed` after ~0.4–1.5 s.
Via the real IP OpenAI answers normally (`401 Unauthorized` without a token — no region block), so the proxy is not needed for this exit.

**Workaround**
Pinning real IPs in the `hosts` file (traffic still goes through the tunnel, just bypassing the proxy) fixes Codex completely.

**Expected behavior**
- Either don't rewrite OpenAI domains for exits where OpenAI is reachable directly, or fix the proxy.
- Respect the "Use AmneziaDNS" switch / custom DNS on Premium, or clearly show in the UI that it is ignored.

Possibly related: #2655, #2375, #2996

issues.title: Release files blocked by GFW
issues.body:
Currently, the release files linked on the download page of amnezia.org are hosted exclusively on Github. As a result, it is impossible to download the client from within China, since the GFW has partially blocked Github. It is entirely possible that Russia would do the same in the future too. 

Therefore, I suggest that the release files be hosted on an alternative site (google storage for example, where the mirror of amnezia.org is hosted) in addition to Github, and a link to the alternative site be provided on amnezia.org so that it remains accessible even when Github is blocked. I hope the workflow needed for this would not be too complicated to set up. 

Currently there is a sourceforge page for amnezia client with download links as well, but it is honestly unclear whether it was set up by the real dev team and whether the release files there are genuine. If the page is official, adding a link to it on amnezia.org would partly address the issue as well, as sourceforge is _as of yet_ not blocked by GFW. However, a lower traffic host with lower risk of being blocked would be better, in my opinion.

issues.title: Split tunneling does not work for griffini.ru — video playback blocked by geo-restriction/VPN detection despite domain rules
issues.body: **Describe the bug** When split tunneling is enabled with a list of griffin.ru domains (via custom JSON file `griffini_amnezia.json` or site rules), playing any episode on https://griffini.ru still triggers a geo-restriction error in the video player: > "Контент недоступен в вашем регионе (AE). Пожалуйста, используйте VPN или смените страну." The site continues to detect VPN usage (or inconsistent routing), and the episode does not play. This happens even though: - VPN is connected to a self-hosted server in the Netherlands - Split tunneling is configured for griffini.ru domains - The goal is to route the necessary traffic through the VPN so the site works correctly **To Reproduce** 1. Go to https://griffini.ru 2. In AmneziaVPN enable split tunneling and add all griffin.ru-related domains (using [griffini_amnezia.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29600092/griffini_amnezia.json) or equivalent site-based rules). 3. Connect to the VPN server. 4. Play any episode. 5. The video player shows the region/VPN detection error and playback fails. **Expected behavior** Split tunneling should properly route **all** required traffic for griffin.ru (including subdomains, APIs, video CDNs and streaming endpoints) through the VPN tunnel. The site should then work without triggering the geo-restriction or VPN detection. **Actual behavior** The geo-restriction error persists. It looks like not all necessary connections are being routed through the VPN (possibly because the site uses many additional domains/IPs for video delivery that are not covered by the current split tunneling rules). **Log files** [AmneziaVPN (client log).log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29600158/AmneziaVPN.client.log.log) [AmneziaVPN (service log).log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29600157/AmneziaVPN.service.log.log) **Screenshots** Attached (shows the video player error while VPN is connected and split tunneling is enabled for griffini.ru domains). **Desktop (please complete the following information):** - OS: Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200.8737) - Version: 4.8.19.0 **Additional context** - VPN type: Self-hosted server (Netherlands) - The website hosts a large collection of Family Guy episodes dubbed in Russian. - I have not tested this on other websites. - This may be related to how site-based split tunneling resolves domains to IPs (only one IP per domain, no automatic updates, etc.).

issues.title: Предлагаю руководству AmneziaVPN либо ограничить халяву, либо полностью её обрезать.
issues.body:
Суть предложения в следующем: прекратить использовать платных подписчиков компании для предоставления безлимитного доступа людям, которым нравится пользоваться социальными сетями за чужой счет и которые, судя по всему, не собираются платить за услугу — даже в отдаленном будущем (путем перехода на платный тариф). Зачем мне платить за доступ из собственного кармана каким-то загадочным личностям, когда даже на Премиум-плане YouTube загружает видео в качестве 360p с ужасной буферизацией в часы пик? Если политика и бизнес-модель компании по-прежнему ориентированы на саморекламу с бесплатным и неограниченным доступом к социальным сетям в надежде, что, возможно, кто-то купит подписку, я отвечу прямо — нет, не будут. Потому что с отправкой фотографий в Telegram и на другие платформы у них и так все в порядке. Им более чем достаточно бесплатного доступа к мессенджерам и социальным сетям. Пришло время перейти от «компании для гиков» к респектабельному VPN-провайдеру: неделя-две пробного доступа — нравится — платите; если нет такого желания, заблудитесь и прекратите перегружать сетевую инфраструктуру.

Наверняка Amnezia знакома с реализацией бизнес-модели по предоставлению услуги VPN компании Adguard: 3 ГБ в месяц на полной скорости, после исчерпания лимитированного трафика скорость урезается до 512 Кбит/с. Так почему бы не поступить таким же образом? Для просмотра фото и написания текста данной скорости должно хватить нищим и жадным троллюшкам.

issues.title: docs: add "Community Tools" section linking CLI/headless install solutions
issues.body:
Hi team,

Following up on Discussion #2356 (15 Mar, 4 upvotes), which has been open without a maintainer reply for about 35 days. Filing as an Issue with the `documentation` label per the repo's existing classification — hopefully easier to triage than an [Ideas] discussion.

**Why a docs section is worth it**

A repeating pattern shows up across this repo and adjacent forums — users want CLI / headless AmneziaWG on Linux servers, separate from the desktop client:

- #850 "Headless installation & CLI interface?" — 81 reactions, open since June 2024
- Discussion #2124 "Debian 13 / Kernel Module tutorial"
- Discussion #2470 "client-to-client over AWG2.0 own VPS" — Q&A, 13 days silence
- forum.qubes-os.org/t/39005 — 2.4k views
- Same questions surface in Reddit r/AmneziaVPN and ntc.party

Right now docs.amnezia.org doesn't point readers anywhere for self-hosted server setup, so people reinvent the wheel.

**Concrete proposal**

Add a short "Community Tools" section under the existing server docs. Draft:

> **Community Tools**
>
> For Linux administrators who prefer command-line setup over the desktop client, the community maintains several tools:
>
> - **amneziawg-installer** (Bash, Ubuntu/Debian + ARM) — one-command kernel-native server install with client management, vpn:// QR import, mobile-carrier DPI preset
> - **amneziawg-go** — userspace implementation for environments without kernel modules (LXC, restricted hosts)
> - **amneziawg-tools** — `awg` / `awg-quick` CLI utilities

**Affiliation**

I maintain amneziawg-installer (one of the tools listed). Happy to submit a PR with this section + descriptions, or just provide the content for your team to integrate.

issues.title: QR import format for AmneziaWG profiles
issues.body:
Hi team,  
We’re running a **self‑hosted AmneziaWG server on a VPS**. Importing the `.conf` file into the iOS app works correctly. However, when we generate a QR code ourselves (using Python to convert the `.conf` → JSON → zlib → base64), the app always fails with **error 900**. The logs show:

```
qUncompress: Input data is corrupted
stopDecodingQr
```

We verified that:

- The QR payload base64‑decodes correctly  
- zlib decompresses correctly  
- The resulting JSON is valid  
- The structure matches what we see in the app’s own backup export  

But the app still imports an **empty profile**.

To avoid further guesswork, could you clarify:

**1. The exact JSON schema required for QR import (fields, types, nesting).  
2. Whether `last_config` must be a JSON **string** or **object**.  
3. Whether `config` must contain the full WG config as a string.  
4. Which AWG fields are required for **manual private VPN** setups.  
5. A minimal valid QR payload example for AmneziaWG.**

This would help us generate QR codes fully compatible with the app for self‑hosted private VPN setups.

Thanks!

issues.body:
One way to start the AmneziaVPN service


Get under sudo:

`sudo -s`

Next, make a sh to start and a directory:

`mkdir -p /etc/sv/amnezia`

`nano /etc/sv/amnezia/run`

```
#!/bin/sh

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/AmneziaVPN/client/lib

exec chpst -u root /opt/AmneziaVPN/service/AmneziaVPN-service.sh
```

Make it executable:
```
chmod +x /etc/sv/AmneziaVPN/run
```
Then link it:
```
ln -s /etc/sv/AmneziaVPN /var/service/
```

[Windows 11 26H2] Built-in AmneziaWG fails with WSAEFAULT, while standalone AmneziaWG 3.1.0 works
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The AmneziaWG connection built into AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 fails on Windows 11 26H2.

The tunnel interface is created successfully, but the client cannot send or receive UDP packets. The service log repeatedly reports errors from `WSASendMsg` and `WSARecvMsg`:

```text
wsasendmsg: The system detected an invalid pointer address in attempting to use a pointer argument in a call.

wsarecvmsg: The system detected an invalid pointer address in attempting to use a pointer argument in a call.
```

As a result, the AmneziaWG handshake never completes.

## Environment

- AmneziaVPN: 5.0.3.0
- Windows: Windows 11 26H2
- Windows build: 26300
- Architecture: x64
- Wintun: 0.14
- Protocol: AmneziaWG
- Standalone AmneziaWG for Windows: 3.1.0

## Troubleshooting performed

I tried the following without success:

- Rebooted the laptop
- Disabled split tunneling
- Disabled Kill Switch
- Confirmed that ByeDPI and Zapret are not installed
- Confirmed that DNS settings are obtained automatically through DHCP
- Flushed and renewed the network configuration
- Checked the Winsock catalog
- Checked installed network filters
- Confirmed that AdGuard and other third-party Winsock providers are not installed

The same AmneziaWG configuration works correctly:

- On a mobile phone connected to the same Wi-Fi network
- In standalone AmneziaWG for Windows 3.1.0 on the same laptop

This confirms that the server, configuration, Wi-Fi connection, UDP connectivity, and MTU are working correctly.

## Additional observations

AmneziaVPN automatically sets the tunnel MTU to 1376. The failure occurs before the first UDP handshake packet can be sent, so changing the MTU or DNS settings does not appear relevant.

Standalone AmneziaWG 3.1.0 works correctly with exactly the same configuration on the same Windows installation.

This strongly suggests a regression or incompatibility in the AmneziaWG tunnel implementation bundled with AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 on Windows 11 26H2.

## Workaround

I currently use standalone AmneziaWG for Windows for AWG connections. AmneziaVPN can still be used for VLESS.

Logs attached.

[AmneziaVPN.essentials.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33356106/AmneziaVPN.essentials.log)

issues.title: Xray/REALITY: `dest` is always default and never follows the SNI set in the UI
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

For an Xray (VLESS + REALITY) container, the generated server config always contains

```json
"dest": "www.googletagmanager.com:443"
```

regardless of what the user configures. The **Server Name (SNI)** field on the Xray security settings page writes only to `serverNames`. There is no UI control for the masking site that `dest` is derived from, so `dest` permanently keeps its built-in default while `serverNames` follows the user's input.

The result is a `dest` and `serverNames` mismatch that the user cannot fix from the app and is never warned about.

**Why it's a problem**

REALITY relays the TLS handshake of every incoming connection to the configured target site, and an unauthenticated visitor is served that site (`dest` is the legacy name of that field, current Xray-core documents it as `target` and treats the two as aliases).

The [official REALITY documentation](https://xtls.github.io/en/config/transports/reality.html) states that `serverNames` has to be consistent with it:

> Usually this should stay consistent with `target`. In practice, valid values are any SNI accepted by the server according to the behavior of `target`, and typically refer to the SAN values on the returned certificate.

The config this app generates cannot satisfy that, because the two fields are driven by different inputs and only one of them is reachable from the UI.

With the mismatch in place, an active prober that connects to the server's IP with the configured SNI is forwarded to `www.googletagmanager.com`, which does not serve that name. It answers with an unrelated Google certificate or fails the handshake — exactly the anomaly REALITY exists to avoid. The whole point of choosing a masking site is defeated, and the user believes they have chosen one because the app offered them a field.

The mismatch does not break authorized clients, since the REALITY client authenticates via the REALITY signature rather than by validating the certificate chain against the SNI. That is why the problem is silent.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Add a self-hosted server, install the **Xray** container.
2. Open the protocol settings, set **Server Name (SNI)** to any domain other than the default, e.g. `example.com`.
3. Save.
4. On the server, read the generated config from inside the container:
   ```
   sudo docker exec amnezia-xray cat /opt/amnezia/xray/server.json
   ```
**Actual behavior**

```json
"realitySettings": {
    "dest": "www.googletagmanager.com:443",
    "fingerprint": "chrome",
    "privateKey": "...",
    "serverNames": ["example.com"],
    "shortIds": ["..."]
}
```

`dest` and `serverNames` refer to two unrelated sites.

**Expected behavior**

Either of:

- `dest` follows the configured name, so the generated config is self-consistent; or
- the masking site is exposed as its own UI field next to SNI, with validation that the entered SNI is served by the chosen `dest`.

At minimum the app should not silently produce a config whose `dest` and `serverNames` disagree.

**Notes from the code**

Not a diagnosis, just what turned up while looking for a workaround. Line references point at the `5.0.1.5` tag; the same code is present in current `dev`.

- `dest` is built from `XrayServerConfig::site`, `serverNames` from `XrayServerConfig::sni` - two independent fields ([`xrayConfigurator.cpp#L418-L425`](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/5.0.1.5/client/core/configurators/xrayConfigurator.cpp#L418-L425)). Both are seeded with the same default at container creation ([`installerBase.cpp#L87`](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/5.0.1.5/client/core/installers/installerBase.cpp#L87)).
- `SiteRole` exists in the model, but no QML page binds it and `grep -rn "site" client/ui/qml/Pages2/PageProtocolXray*.qml` returns nothing. The only exposed field is `Server Name (SNI)` → `SniRole` ([`PageProtocolXraySecuritySettings.qml#L275`](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/5.

issues.title: [Android] Per-app split tunneling bypass via unauthenticated local SOCKS5 listener on 127.0.0.1:10808
issues.body:
**Summary**

When AmneziaVPN is active on Android (X-ray profile), it exposes a SOCKS5 listener on 127.0.0.1:10808 that accepts unauthenticated connections. Because Android loopback is shared across apps, another application can connect to this listener. As a result, an app excluded from VPN routing via per-app split tunneling can still send traffic through the VPN by using the local SOCKS5 proxy. This behavior may unintentionally weaken the isolation guarantees of split tunneling and could increase the detectability of VPN usage in environments where app-level network monitoring is employed.


**Environment** 
- **App version**: 4.8.14.5
- **Android version**: 15
- **Device**: Samsung Galaxy S25
- **Protocol used**: Xray
- **Split tunneling**: Enabled (Termux excluded from VPN)

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install AmneziaVPN and configure a working connection.
2. Enable **Per-app VPN** (split tunneling) and **exclude Termux** (or any test app with `INTERNET` permission).
3. Connect to the VPN.
4. In Termux, run:
   ```bash
   # Verify that direct traffic is not using the VPN
   curl -s https://ifconfig.me/ip
   # Expected: your real public IP
   
   # Check whether the localhost proxy is reachable
   nc -vz -w1 127.0.0.1 10808
   # Observed: connection succeeds only while VPN is active
   
   # Send traffic through the local SOCKS5 proxy from excluded app
   curl -s --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:10808 --connect-timeout 10 https://ifconfig.me/ip
   # Observed: VPN exit IP

**Observed behavior**
- Port `127.0.0.1:10808` is open **only when VPN is active**.
- The listener accepts SOCKS5 connections without authentication.
- An app excluded from VPN routing can still reach the VPN exit by using this localhost proxy.

**Expected Behavior**
Applications excluded from VPN routing should not be able to send traffic through the VPN tunnel via a localhost proxy, unless this behavior is explicitly documented and user-controlled. If a local listener is required for internal purposes, access should be restricted to the app's own components.

**Security Impact**
If the proxy accepts unauthenticated connections and forwards traffic through the VPN tunnel:
- User-configured per-app routing policies can be bypassed by any app with INTERNET permission.
- Traffic that the user explicitly intended to route directly may leak through the VPN (or vice versa).
- The presence of an open, unauthenticated localhost proxy may serve as a detectable signal of VPN usage to monitoring applications.

**Operational relevance**
In environments where applications or platforms monitor network behavior for signs of VPN usage, this issue may increase the detectability of VPN use. Because an app excluded from VPN routing can still access the VPN tunnel via localhost, it can both infer that the VPN is active and send probe traffic through the tunnel. This may also aid enumeration of VPN egress IPs and contribute to blocking of VPN endpoints. This consideration is particularly relevant given recent reports of app-level VPN detection guidelines being distributed to IT platforms [1][2].

**Suggested Mitigations**
- Require SOCKS5 authentication (username/password) for the localhost listener, if the feature is intended for external use.
- If the listener is only needed for internal IPC, consider using a private communication channel (e.g., Unix domain socket with restrictive permissions, or Android Binder with UID verification) instead of a shared TCP port on loopback.
- Document the behavior and its implications in the app's settings or security notes, so users can make informed decisions about split tunneling usage.


**References**
1. **Technical analysis of localhost proxy bypass in mobile VPN clients** (Russian):  
   https://habr.com/ru/articles/1020080/
   
2. **Community discussion: MinDigital guidelines for VPN detection** (Russian):  
   https://habr.com/ru/news/1019646/  
   *Summary: Russian Ministry of Digital Development issued guide

issues.title: [Android] Включить по умолчанию Split tunneling с исключением из туннеля приложений банков, операторов связи и маркетплейсов
issues.body:
Во многих VPN клиентах есть такая фича - предустановленная по умолчанию маршрутизация российских сервисов (банки, Ozon, WB и т.п.) напрямую мимо туннеля. Поскольку некоторые приложения пытаются определить наличие VPN и проверяют доступ к некоторым заблокированным в России сайтам, логичнее было бы пойти дальше - составить список хорошо известных российских приложений и по умолчанию сразу после установки включать split tunneling таким образом, чтобы они были исключены из туннеля. comments.issue_title: [Windows] Kill Switch blocks AmneziaWG handshake — endless "Connecting", tunnel never comes up, DNS/Internet blocked on all adapters
comments.body:
### Update after enabling service logging (2026-11-17 ~18:45 local)

Re-tested with **Kill Switch enabled** and logging on: the same server connected successfully and the tunnel stays up. So the failure is **not deterministic**, and the earlier "Kill Switch blocks the AmneziaWG handshake" hypothesis is not supported by the new logs.

Successful-connection sequence (`C:\ProgramData\AmneziaVPN\log\AmneziaVPN-service.log`, endpoint/peer redacted):

```text
WindowsFirewall : Enabling Killswitch Using Adapter: 54
WindowsFirewall : Filter added:  Allow usage of VPN Adapter : Allow out traffic on Adapter 54
WindowsFirewall : Filter added:  Allow DHCP Traffic : Allow Outbound DHCP
WindowsFirewall : Filter added:  Allow all for AmneziaVPN.exe : Permit (out) IPv4 Traffic of: AmneziaVPN-service
WindowsFirewall : Filter added:  Block all DNS : Block outgoing v4 on Port 53
...
WindowsFirewall : Killswitch on! Rules: 20
WindowsRouteMonitor : Adding exclusion route for <server-ip>/32
WindowsFirewall : Enabling traffic for peer <peer>
WindowsFirewall : Filter added:  Block Internet : Block traffic to 0.0.0.0/0
WindowsFirewall : Filter added:  Allow DNS-Server : Permit traffic to 1.1.1.1 on port 53
WindowsFirewall : excludedAddresses range:  <server-ip>
WindowsFirewall : Filter added:  Allow Ecxlude route : Permit traffic to <server-ip>/32
WireguardUtilsWindows : Configuring peer <peer> via <server-ip>
tunnel.dll : [TUN] [AmneziaVPN] peer(...) - Sending handshake initiation
tunnel.dll : [TUN] [AmneziaVPN] peer(...) - Received handshake response
```

Note `Permit (out) IPv4 Traffic of: AmneziaVPN-service` and the explicit permit for `<server-ip>/32`: the service process **is** allowed and the endpoint is excluded before the handshake. In this run Kill Switch did not block the handshake, and NCSI reported `ActiveHttpProbeSucceeded` on the tunnel adapter ~4 s later.

### Revised assessment

The earlier failures (17:19, 17:52, 17:59) are most consistent with the tunnel itself failing to establish (server/DPI transient) while Kill Switch did what it is designed to do: fail closed. The remaining issues are about recovery and diagnostics:

1. **No rollback/timeout when the tunnel fails**: the client stays in "Connecting" indefinitely and all DNS/Internet remains blocked until the user manually disconnects (or reboots). It should time out, roll back the WFP/DNS changes, and/or clearly offer "disable Kill Switch" instead of leaving the machine offline.
2. **Route monitor defects** in the same successful log:
   - `Adding exclusion route for /999999` → `Failed to update route: 87` (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) — an invalid prefix is produced while parsing the configuration.
   - `Failed to update route: 5010` (ERROR_OBJECT_ALREADY_EXISTS) for `172.25.64.0/20`, `172.30.208.0/20` and `192.168.0.0/24` when "capturing" local routes.
3. **LAN breakage**: the same log captures `192.168.0.0/24`, `172.25.64.0/20`, `172.30.208.0/20` and the resulting table routes them via the tunnel, so the local router/Docker/WSL become unreachable while connected (cf. #2830). Separate from Kill Switch, but visible in the same session.

I can attach the full service log (27 KB, keys and endpoint redacted) if you tell me the preferred way. Logging is now enabled, so if the failure recurs I will capture the failing attempt as well.

comments.issue_title: [Feature Request] Add "on demand" activation of VPN
comments.body:
Hi! I'd like to implement this for **iOS and macOS (the Network Extension build)** and open a PR against `dev`. Before writing code I want to check that the approach works for you.

**Proposal**
- Use the native `NEOnDemandRule`s on the `NETunnelProviderManager` that `IosController` already saves, so the system brings the tunnel up even when the app isn't running. The extension already starts from `providerConfiguration` alone (AWG/WireGuard, OpenVPN, XRay), so `PacketTunnelProvider` needs no changes.
- App-wide settings, applied to the tunnel of the selected server:
  - Connect on demand: on / off
  - On cellular: connect / do nothing
  - On Wi-Fi: connect / do nothing
  - Trusted Wi-Fi networks (SSIDs typed in by the user): disconnect
- A manual disconnect in the app turns on-demand off for that profile, otherwise iOS reconnects right away. The next connect turns it back on, the same way the WireGuard iOS app does it.
- The settings are hidden on other platforms.

**Questions**
1. Would you accept a PR like this?
2. Where should the settings live, and is there a Figma design for them? If not, I'd build a page under Application settings from the existing `Controls2` components.
3. I can't sign Network Extension builds for a device myself. Could the PR be checked through your TestFlight build?

Related: #2672, #2987.

comments.issue_title: [Windows 11 26H2] Built-in AmneziaWG fails with WSAEFAULT, while standalone AmneziaWG 3.1.0 works
comments.body:
Additional reproduction on AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6 / Windows build 26300.

Environment:
- Windows 10 Pro reported by Get-ComputerInfo, build 26300
- AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6
- AmneziaWG 3.1
- Ethernet, native IPv6 enabled
- Split tunneling disabled
- Endpoint: [123:123:123:123::1]:48705
- AllowedIPs: 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0

The same AWG profile works on Android through the same router and ISP.
Windows can ping the IPv6 endpoint and TCP/22 succeeds.
Find-NetRoute selects the physical Ethernet interface, not the VPN interface.

The imported configuration is valid and contains:
- Jc/Jmin/Jmax
- S1-S4 and H1-H4
- HeaderProtectionKey
- ContentPaddingAddition
- PersistentKeepalive
- IPv6 endpoint with brackets

However, while AmneziaVPN remains stuck at "Connecting...", tcpdump on the router sees zero UDP packets from the Windows host to port 48705. The phone sends bidirectional UDP traffic successfully ON THE SAME ADMIN CONFIG.

This means the failure happens before the first packet leaves the Windows client.

Please check the Windows tunnel backend around WSASendMsg/WSARecvMsg and the fallback after RIO initialization. If WSAEFAULT occurs, the client should:
1. log the exact socket error;
2. stop the tunnel with a visible error instead of spinning forever;
3. fall back to plain sendto/recvfrom where possible;
4. verify WSAMSG/WSABUF/control-buffer lifetime and alignment.
